hints: Focus on what hydrolysis does to a bromoalkane, it simply swaps each C-Br for C-OH without moving the carbon skeleton.
Write out 2,3-dibromohexane as $\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCHBrCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and see that only carbons 2 and 3 can gain OH groups.
Check each option to see where the OH groups are, the one with OH groups on carbons other than 2 and 3 cannot form from this starting material.
walkthrough:
**Draw the starting material**

Think side by side with me. 2,3-dibromohexane means a 6-carbon chain with Br on C2 and C3.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCHBrCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$

**Recall partial and complete hydrolysis**

Hydrolysis with water replaces C-Br with C-OH by nucleophilic substitution. Partial means only one Br is replaced. Complete means both Br are replaced.

$$\text{R-Br + H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{R-OH + HBr}$$

**Predict the possible products**

Partial gives two possibilities: OH on C2 with Br left on C3, or Br left on C2 with OH on C3. Complete gives OH on both C2 and C3.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CHBrCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \text{ and } \text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$

**Spot the impossible structure**

A 3,4-diol has OH groups on C3 and C4. Our starting material never had Br on C4, so this cannot form. That is the species not present.

options.A: This is present. It is one partial hydrolysis product with OH on C2 and Br still on C3, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CHBrCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Since the question asks for what is not present, this is not the answer.
options.B: This is present. It is the complete hydrolysis product, the 2,3-diol $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, formed when both Br atoms on C2 and C3 are replaced by OH.
options.C: This is not present and so is correct. It is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, a 3,4-diol. It would require Br on C3 and C4 in the starting material, but we started with 2,3-dibromohexane, so it cannot form.
options.D: This is present. It looks different but read it from the right: $\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. It is the other partial hydrolysis product with Br on C2 and OH on C3.
